x-bump-note: 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0 declares the optional `execution_basis` scalar — the basis a review's verdict rests on: "executed" (the reviewer ran something) or "read-only" (the verdict rests on reading only). Requested by claude-klabauter-em (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-11-claude-klabauter-em-review-trail-execution-basis-field.md), whose `chain_partition_verdict_discharged` discharges a mandatory review scale against records carrying no execution information, so a reviewer that ran nothing and one that ran the suite discharge identically across 1804 state/review-trail/ records. The producing half is already live on this side (2cb87e464): `coordinator:code-reviewer`'s return line carries `executed: <yes|no>` and every review-findings sidecar fills a `## Execution capability` section — that fact was emitted on every dispatch and thrown away at the trail boundary for want of a field. Sender's proposed shape adopted verbatim, including two enum values rather than three: absence already carries "unknown", so an explicit third value would be a state needing byte-distinction from absence for no named consumer. Classified nested-field-additive, NOT major, per schema-version-gate.md § Bump-class extension key: a new OPTIONAL top-level scalar on the existing review-trail entity, narrowing no declared domain — `required` is unchanged and the schema has no `additionalProperties: false`, so every one of the existing records keeps validating. Canonical-first rather than vendored-ahead-pin: the two copies were converged at bump time (this SSOT's 1.2.0 at 840491558109540f7416e6f09c78148f336873ec, claude-klabauter's vendored byte-pin at the same SHA), and the ahead-pin registry — for which review-trail is itself the worked example, from 2026-08-10 — documents its empty state as the healthy one. The DR-097 push-side notification duty attaches to a vendored-schema bump of any class and is discharged by the reply memo to claude-klabauter-em, who re-vendor via bin/claude-klabauter-revendor-schema.py and move their pin. NEGATIVE SPEC: no gate-behaviour change rides along — an unexecuted review keeps discharging, and whether that ever changes is a PM decision the sender deliberately left open pending measurement. PRIOR: 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0 closes `scope_kind` from a bare unconstrained string to an explicit enum: ["diff", "plan", "integration"] — the exact set both consumer copies of `_credit_from_kind_partition` (coordinator_core/coverage.py, coordinator_core/ops/review_coverage_core.py) actually handle. This change originated on the vendored copy in claude-klabauter (commit 55cbf4ede) and never reached this SSOT until now: before the bump the schema admitted ANY string — its own description even named "chunk" as an example — while the consumer asserted on a closed set, so one hand-authored record with an out-of-set scope_kind (observed: "chunk", "inline-dispatch") took down the whole coverage gate with an AssertionError before it ever reached a VERDICT line. Classified `major` per this schema's own house vocabulary (a value NARROWING, from unconstrained to closed, is the more restrictive direction — a document valid under 1.1.0 with e.g. scope_kind:"chunk" no longer validates under 1.2.0). Fixed the misleading description at the same time — it cited "chunk" as an example scope_kind despite no consumer ever crediting it. "chunk" is NOT added as a fourth enum value at this bump: whether it should ever be creditable is a policy call outside this fix's scope. 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0 added the optional `reviewed_paths` array — the path set a scope_kind:diff review actually covered, so a record attests coverage instead of implying it from its sha_range time window.
description: Review-trail record — one JSON document per code-review event, written under state/review-trail/*.json (whole-document match; the record IS the whole JSON file, not frontmatter). The 8 original fields are all required; `reviewed_paths` (present only on scope_kind:diff records) and `execution_basis` are optional.

sha_range.description: Git commit SHA range covered by this review (e.g. 'abc1234..def5678').

reviewer.description: Identifier of the reviewer (agent persona or worker) that produced this review.

scope.description: Description or path set identifying what was reviewed.

scope_kind.description: Category of the reviewed scope. "diff" credits its resolved SHAs unconditionally; "plan" credits only the subset independently classified as planning-artifact commits; "integration" is a recognized shape that is always skipped (never credited). No other value is accepted — the closed set both live consumer copies of _credit_from_kind_partition (coordinator_core/coverage.py, coordinator_core/ops/review_coverage_core.py) actually handle.

diff_loc.description: Lines of diff covered by this review.

session_id.description: Identifier of the session that produced this review record.

workstream.description: Workstream identifier associated with this review, or null when not attributed to a specific workstream.

reviewed_paths.description: Optional set of paths this record's review actually covered (e.g. from freeze-review-diff.py --paths), or null when not supplied. Present only on scope_kind:diff records; omitted on plan/integration records. Exists because sha_range is a time window, not a path set: on a shared branch a record written as <my-first-commit>^..HEAD silently confers coverage on every concurrent peer session's commit inside the window. The write-side refusal guard is the enforcement; this key is the honest attestation.

execution_basis.description: Optional basis on which this review's verdict rests: "executed" — the reviewer ran something (tests, a probe, the CLI under review); "read-only" — the verdict rests on reading only. Omitted when not determined; absence means unknown and is never equivalent to "read-only".
